english: my heart was in my mouth
also: my heart was in my throat

terms.gloss: my breath was in my nose: I was terrified
evidence: Petron. 62: mihi anima in nāsō esse, stābam tamquam mortuus
terms.comment: Literally “my breath was in my nose”: the breath has risen to leave the body. Petronius gives it to a freedman at Trimalchio’s dinner, frightened stiff; it is everyday, not literary, Latin.
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Petr. (a freedman telling a ghost story)

sources: Lewis & Short: anima · Lewis & Short: nasus
